findings.summary: Step 1 says the change will "continue" rejecting absolute paths and traversal, but those rejections live only in `ScopeFence.allows` (`scope.py:45-56`, `_escapes_the_repository`), not in the resolution code that remains. After removing the fence, `read_reference` keeps only `target.relative_to(root)`, which rejects paths that escape the repository but accepts an absolute path that lands inside the repo (`repo_root / "/abs/in/repo"` discards `repo_root` and still resolves under root) and accepts in-repo traversal such as `src/../.ai/context.md`. The plan therefore promises a property its described edit does not deliver, and step 3's test "verify traversal, absolute paths ... remain rejected" would fail against the plan's own implementation.
findings.evidence_required: Plan text naming the explicit replacement check added to `read_reference` (e.g. reuse of `_escapes_the_repository` or an equivalent reject-if-absolute / reject-if-`..`-in-parts guard applied before resolution), plus a stated expected outcome for each of: absolute path inside the repo, absolute path outside, `../` escaping, and `src/../<excluded>` staying inside.

findings.summary: The plan is framed entirely around paths "excluded from modification scope", but the repository's own failure for `AGENTS.md` is not exclusion — `.ai/project.yaml` `scope.include` is `[src/, tests/, docs/, README.md, pyproject.toml]`, so `AGENTS.md` fails the *include* test, while `.ai/context.md` fails the *exclude* test. An implementer who reads step 1 narrowly ("permit declared references even when excluded") and only bypasses the exclude list will still silently drop `AGENTS.md`, i.e. half the brief's named deliverable, and the plan's step 5 acceptance wording would not catch it.
findings.evidence_required: Plan text stating that read authorization no longer consults include *or* exclude for declared references, plus a test fixture whose `scope.include` does not cover the persistent path (mirroring the real `.ai/project.yaml`) asserting `AGENTS.md` loads as an invariant.

findings.summary: Removing the fence also removes the post-resolution check at `assembler.py:206-210`, which is what stops a declared reference from being redirected via symlink. Declared reference paths live under agent-writable trees (`docs/`, `src/` are in `include`), so a run can replace a declared reference with a symlink to `.git/config` or `.ai/runs/<prior run>` and have that content read into the next run's prompt. This stays inside the repository, so neither the plan's remaining containment check nor its step 5 criterion ("no reference resolving outside the repository") detects it. The plan proposes no replacement guard and does not record the trade-off.
findings.evidence_required: Either a decision recorded in the plan that in-repo symlink redirection of declared references is acceptable (with a test pinning the new behaviour), or a specified mitigation — e.g. a read deny-list for `.git/`, or requiring the resolved path to equal `repo_root / rel_path`.

findings.summary: The plan deletes a control the spec of record declares. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-25-dev-orchestration-v1-design.md:190` lists "Context assembly — excluded paths are never read, and never reach an agent prompt" as enforcement point 1 of three independent enforcement places, and `docs/.../2026-08-29-m2-the-loop.md:860` codes it as such. The brief forbids changes outside `src/` and `tests/`, so the plan leaves the spec asserting a false invariant with no escalation, while AGENTS.md requires escalation on changes crossing a security boundary and the active profile sets `workflow_changes_review_required: true`.
findings.evidence_required: Explicit acknowledgement in the plan that enforcement point 1 is being retired, plus either an approved scope extension to amend §6 of the design spec or a recorded decision (run artifact / escalation) accepting the documentation divergence under the current scope restriction.

findings.summary: Step 3's "preserve coverage" list omits the two existing assertions that encode the opposite invariant and must be retired: `test_read_reference_refuses_a_path_outside_the_fence` (tests/context/test_assembler.py:46-52) and the second assertion of `test_reference_symlinks_cannot_escape_root_or_fence` (line 73-74, symlink to an excluded in-repo file). The plan reads as purely additive, so an executor following it will hit unexplained failures and may "fix" them by weakening the escape assertions in the same test.
findings.evidence_required: Plan text enumerating each existing assertion being deleted or rewritten, with the replacement assertion for each, and confirmation that the outside-the-repo symlink assertion (line 71-72) is retained unchanged.

findings.summary: The plan does not state whether the `fence` parameter is removed from the signatures or retained and ignored, and does not account for the mechanical ripple: `runner.py:322`, `tests/context/test_assembler.py:50/58/72/74/102/133`, `tests/workflow/test_bootstrap.py:99`. It also leaves `from dev_orchestration.scope import ScopeFence` unused at `assembler.py:7`, which `ruff check` will fail as F401 — one of the plan's own step 4 gates.
findings.evidence_required: Plan text stating the final signatures of `read_reference` and `resolve_runtime_context`, the list of call sites updated, and removal of the now-unused `ScopeFence` import from `assembler.py`.
